title: Per-Page Layouts & Nested Layouts
description: Assign different layouts to different pages and nest them for complex UIs.

slides.title: One Layout Doesn't Fit All 🎭
slides.content:
# Different Pages, Different Needs

The dashboard might need a sidebar; the marketing page might need a hero banner.

A single layout in `_app.js` is too rigid.

**Solution: Per‑Page Layouts.**

You can define a `getLayout` function on each page, and `_app.js` uses it to wrap that page.

This keeps the layout logic close to the page and allows unlimited customization.

slides.title: The getLayout Pattern (pages/_app.js)
slides.content: Check if the page has a getLayout method; if so, use it. Otherwise, fall back to a default layout or just the page.

quizData.question: What is the benefit of defining a `getLayout` function on a page?

options.text: It allows each page to specify its own layout component without changing `_app.js`
It forces all pages to use the same layout
It only works with the App Router

quizData.explanation: The getLayout pattern decouples layout logic from the App component, giving each page full control over its surrounding UI.

slides.title: Page with a Custom Layout (pages/dashboard.js)
slides.content: Export a `getLayout` function along with the component.

slides.title: Nested Layouts – The App Router Way 📁
slides.content:
# In the App Router (next/app)

Next.js 13+ introduced the `app` directory with a more powerful layout system:

* `layout.js` files automatically wrap child routes.
* You can nest layouts infinitely.
* Layouts preserve state across navigations.

```
app/
  layout.js          // Root layout (required)
  dashboard/
    layout.js        // Dashboard-specific layout
    page.js
```

This approach is now recommended for new projects, but the Pages Router `getLayout` still works great for existing codebases.

slides.title: App Router Example (app/layout.js)
slides.content: A root layout with a global nav and a `{children}` slot for page content.

quizData.question: In the App Router, what is the primary advantage of nested layouts?

options.text: They reduce the number of files
Child layouts preserve their state when navigating between sibling routes
They eliminate the need for JavaScript

quizData.explanation: In the App Router, layouts are persistent. Navigating from `/dashboard/settings` to `/dashboard/analytics` keeps the dashboard layout mounted, preserving state like scroll position or form inputs.
